chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Washing the two hands before eating and after it increases longevity, removes stains from clothing, and clarifies the vision.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of washing hands before and after eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration, recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, traces a saying of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) back to Amir Al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), emphasizing the spiritual and physical hygiene of washing hands before and after meals. The hadith highlights three specific virtues: increased longevity, removal of stains from clothing, and improved eyesight, reflecting the holistic approach to health in Shia tradition. This practice is often linked to the concept of *barakah* in sustenance and the purification of the body as a vessel for the soul.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Washing the two hands before the meal and after it increases in the age, and the removing for the stains from the clothing, and it stimulates the vision’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather Hisham ibn Salim ibn Rashid from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu’minin has said, ‘
Washing hands before and after eating food removes stains from clothes and clears eyesight.’”
